purpose: Census of what the trust-surfaces reference sweep actually found, per surface kind, including the queries that returned nothing usable. Silence is not coverage: a kind with no record here is NOT COVERED, and the queries tried are listed so the next sweep does not repeat them.
source: Mobbin MCP, platform web, mode deep
licenceNote: Zero images were downloaded, cached, embedded, or written to disk. Every record stores our own measurements plus the mobbin_url and the date, per the approved 'mobbin' source policy in shared/nodeslideAtlasRegistry.ts (download false, cache false, ragIndexing false, embeddingIndex false, displayThumbnail true, accessMode remote-mcp, attributionRequired true).

evidenceTierPolicy.reason: Mobbin is a curated gallery. A gallery screen is not a live observation of a running product and carries no audience outcome, so no record in this sweep may be promoted above bronze without re-observing the product live (silver/M2) or attaching an outcome (gold/M3).

queriesUsed: AI writing suggestion card with Accept and Dismiss buttons pending user decision
AI agent proposes edits to a document and the user reviews then accepts or rejects each change (flows)

examinedButNotRecorded.reason: The generated variants carry a percentage badge reading '± 75%' and '± 27%' whose meaning could not be determined from the image. Recording it would have required guessing what the number measures, so the screen was dropped rather than described speculatively.

Three undecided suggestion options render identically with unselected radios, which is an unambiguous confirmation of the decision-colour rule, but every fact it offers is already carried with more detail by obs-air-duplicate-asset-conflict-1 (the same radio-then-confirm pattern, with the counter-instance behaviour). Dropped to avoid a redundant record.

queriesUsed: side by side code diff review with added and removed lines highlighted green and red

examinedButNotRecorded.reason: Its distinctive fact — an entirely empty prior pane for a file with 23 additions and 0 deletions — is carried more informatively by obs-googleaistudio-viewing-differences-1/f4, which draws absence as hatching rather than leaving it blank.

A revision comparison with no background tint on any row, which would have been useful counter-evidence for a colourless diff. Dropped because the change markers in the gutter could not be read clearly enough at the returned resolution to state what distinguishes the two columns, and a diff observation that cannot locate the difference is not an observation.

queriesUsed: cookie consent banner with accept all and reject all buttons and manage preferences link
OAuth authorization screen listing the permissions an app is requesting before you grant access to your account

examinedButNotRecorded.reason: A settings screen for choosing which consent banner to install on your own site. It is a product-configuration surface, not a consent moment, so it does not belong in this kind.

OneTrust preference centre with three of four categories pre-enabled. Its facts duplicate obs-mercor-cookie-purposes-1 and obs-cron-google-oauth-consent-1 exactly; recorded here as a third data point for the pre-granted-defaults count without a full record.
Cookie preferences with all four categories pre-checked and a single Save action. Same duplication as Calendly; counted in the pre-granted-defaults tally, not given its own record.
Cookie settings with all categories pre-checked, each carrying a concrete usage example. Same duplication; counted in the tally.

queriesUsed: error state screen saying something went wrong with a retry button

examinedButNotRecorded.reason: A one-sentence failure with a small black pill retry and nothing else. Counted in the census tallies below; too thin to justify its own record.
Failure illustration drawn in the brand blue with an unfilled Try Again. Counted in the census tallies below; its facts are carried by obs-midday-error-escape-hatch-1 and obs-paypal-error-debug-id-1.

censusAcrossAllFiveFailureScreensExamine.note: Counts cover PayPal, Typeform, Midday, Threads, and VEED. The single identifier is PayPal's Debug ID; the single surviving success marker is Typeform's green completed step.

queriesUsed: version conflict dialog asking user to keep their version or the server version
coverage.whatWasFound: Name-collision resolution (Air) and destructive version rollback (Navattic, Confluence, and Linear's restore path). These are genuine conflict surfaces: a human is asked to choose between two states of the same object.

notCovered.description: No reference was found for the case that matters most to an agentic product: two writers changed the same field, and the surface presents mine / theirs / merged as a three-way choice. Every result for the conflict query resolved to version history and rollback instead.
queriesTried: version conflict dialog asking user to keep their version or the server version
notCovered.consequence: Any NodeKit direction gate touching a concurrent-edit merge surface must declare novel-by-intent. There is no reference in this corpus for it to remix, and citing the rollback records as if they covered merge would be a false citation.

examinedButNotRecorded.reason: Page history with a version list and Restore version / Cancel. Every fact it offers is carried in more detail by obs-linear-version-redline-1, which shows the same pattern with an inline redline and a change stepper.

corpusGaps.detail: Nothing in this sweep shows an agent asking permission before it makes an outbound call, or an agent tool-call reporting its own failure. The consent references are all human-to-application data grants and the failure references are all page-level. Our own product's data-agent-web-consent posture has no external reference behind it.

corpusGaps.gap: no internal counter-observation for the decision-colour violations
corpusGaps.detail: The three decision-colour violations fixed in our own product this week are not recorded anywhere retrievable. Searched parity-studio origin/main and every local branch for trust-surface, proposal-card, pending-accent, and acceptance-colour markers over the last four days and found no commit, doc, or observation. rule-decision-colour-containment therefore cites external counter-evidence only, and names this as an outstanding gap rather than citing an observation id that does not exist.

Every external record in this sweep is M1. No rule built on it may claim that a pattern WORKS — only that shipped products do it. Promotion requires either live re-observation (M2) or an outcome measurement (M3).
